title: Krishna in the best of everything
hookLine: Arjuna asks where to look for Krishna, and the answer runs from the ocean to the first letter, a
carry: vibhuti: god shines in the best of everything
tomorrow: how did a robber become a saint by saying a name backwards?

lines: YOU ARE THE SOURCE OF EVERYTHING.
WHERE DO I LOOK FOR YOU?
cards: In the middle of the Gita, on the battlefield, Arjuna has just heard that his friend and charioteer is the source of everything. So he asks what anyone would ask next. How do I keep you in mind?
In what things should I think of you? Tell me again, he says. I never get tired of hearing it.

teach.h: OCEAN, HIMALAYA, GANGA, THE LETTER A.
teach.b: Krishna answers with a list, one of the loveliest in the Gita. Among waters, I am the ocean. Among things that stand firm, the Himalaya.
Among trees, the sacred fig. Among rivers, the Ganga. And then, in paraphrase: among letters, I am the letter a.
Then he gives the key to the whole list: whatever is glorious, beautiful or mighty, know that it springs from a spark of my splendor. And: I hold up this whole world with one small part of myself.
These are his vibhutis, his shinings: places where the divine shows through most clearly. Here's the teaching. Krishna doesn't say the ocean is all of God.
He says God shines in the best of each kind, so an ocean, a great river or a mountain can lead the mind to him.
That's why a family at the beach may fold their hands to the sea, why the Ganga is bathed in as holy, and why pilgrims walk around Mount Kailasa. Now the letter.
A is the plainest sound there is: open the mouth, let the voice out, don't shape it. A. It's where the Sanskrit alphabet begins.
And in Devanagari, the script Sanskrit is often written in, a consonant carries a short a inside it unless a mark says otherwise. The letter for k is read ka; for m, ma.

teach.h: THE PLAINEST SOUND RUNS THROUGH ALL.
teach.b: So the a runs, quietly, through almost every letter on the page. Many teachers read that as Krishna's point: the divine is the plainest thing, running through everything else.
This week, the sounds of the sacred words, and what they carry.

how: Hindus honor the divine shining in the greatest of each kind, as Krishna lists in Gita 10: bathing in the Ganga, folding hands to the sea, going on pilgrimage to great mountains; students of Sanskrit also learn that the letter a, which Krishna names among letters, sounds inside almost every consonant.

o: a mark that makes a vowel sound twice as long
the plainest letter, the one Krishna names, hidden inside each consonant
the last letter, the closing hum of a chant

s: Krishna names the letter a in the Gita
Gita 10.33: among letters, I am a.
Krishna says the ocean is the whole of God
whatever is glorious springs from a spark of his splendor; he holds the world with one part of himself.
a Devanagari consonant on its own is read with a short a
the letter for k is read ka, unless a mark changes it.

games.q: a friend asks: 'if God is in everything, why bow to the ocean in particular?' by Gita 10, what fits?
o: God shines most clearly in the best of each kind, so the ocean leads the mind to him.
the ocean isn't special; God lives only in temples.
the ocean is all of God, and nothing else is.
games.why: among waters, I am the ocean: whatever is glorious springs from a spark of Krishna's splendor. a shining, not the whole.

practice: Let the jaw soften, breathe in through the nose, and on the out-breath let a quiet, unshaped sound come out: a, like the start of the word about. Let it last as long as the breath, then rest in the silence.
If you pray, let each a be a small bow to the one Krishna says runs through it; if not, just notice where the sound seems to come from. If sound isn't possible where you are, say it inwardly.

wordCard.voice: A. The open mouth, the plainest sound, the letter Krishna names among his shinings, hidden inside almost every letter on the page.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: a, the first letter, the open mouth. Krishna names it in Gita 10.33.
